title: "Operator Quick Start"

This chapter is the shortest safe production sequence. It assumes a reviewed
release checkout and administrator access to the target VM. It does not claim
that VM-side readiness gates have passed.

## Sync the reviewed repository to the VM

The first operator action is to place the reviewed repository state on the
server. This has not been done by the repository delivery itself.

The intended VM workflow is the same source-checkout pattern used for the
BCFMS system: keep the Git repository in the operator home area and update it
there before deploying.

```bash
cd /home/yeroslaviz/BCFPPCF-project-management
git pull origin main
git status --short
```

`git status --short` should be empty for a production release. The checkout
path is the source path later passed to `scripts/deploy.sh --source`.

The PPSV deployment step does not make that home checkout the live Shiny app.
It copies `ppsvf-app/` from the checkout into a new immutable release under
`/srv/ppsvf-app/releases/`, excludes mutable local state such as databases and
`.Renviron`, fixes ownership and permissions, restarts Shiny, and atomically
points `/srv/shiny-server/ppsvf-app` at the new release. This keeps rollback
available while preserving the familiar `git pull origin main` operator flow.

Do not transfer local databases, generated Quarto output, `.Renviron` files,
SMTP secrets, or ad-hoc test uploads. The PPSV deployment must initialize a
fresh database on the VM when one is absent.

## Before touching production

This is an evidence checklist, not a command sequence. Before anyone describes
the VM as production-ready, an operator must know who owns each item below and
where the proof is recorded:

1. The exact TLS private key matching the leaf certificate for
   `ppcf-vm.biochem.mpg.de` is available. A CSR is not a private key.
2. The SMTP administrators have authorized
   `ppsv-service@biochem.mpg.de` for the configured relay account.
3. A real ticket test has established which requester/auto-reply path works
   without duplicate acknowledgements.
4. `PPSV_BACKUP_DIR` is an external destination whose exact `findmnt` source is
   recorded, and the storage team has documented the snapshot/restore policy
   for `/fs/pool/pool-ppsvf-projects`.

The system may be installed while a gate is pending, but it must not be called
production-ready.

## Prepare the runtime environment

Copy the tracked template to a protected temporary operator path, fill every
required value, and keep the real file out of Git:

```bash
sudo install -o root -g root -m 0600 \
  scripts/ppsvf-app.env.example /root/ppsvf-app.env
sudoedit /root/ppsvf-app.env
```

Production invariants are:

```ini
AUTH_MODE=ldap
PPSV_PUBLIC_URL=https://ppcf-vm.biochem.mpg.de/ppsvf-app/
APP_RUN_USER=ppsvf-shiny-user
APP_RUN_GROUP=ppsvf-shiny
PPSV_POOL_GROUP=b_profa
PPSV_DB_FILE=/srv/ppsvf-app-data/ppsv_projects.db
PPSV_POOL_ROOT=/fs/pool/pool-ppsvf-projects
PPSV_FALLBACK_ROOT=/srv/ppsvf-app-data/uploads_pending_pool
PPSV_POOL_EXPECTED_SOURCE=REQUIRED_FACILITY_POOL_MOUNT_SOURCE
PPSV_ALLOW_LOCAL_POOL=0
```

Never put SMTP credentials or another secret in the repository or in an
application-local `.Renviron`. Provisioning installs the environment as
`/etc/ppsvf-app/ppsvf-app.env`, owned by root and mode `0640` or stricter.

Record both external mount sources exactly:

```bash
findmnt -n -o SOURCE -T /fs/pool/pool-ppsvf-projects
findmnt -n -o SOURCE -T /the/configured/backup/path
```

Set those results as `PPSV_POOL_EXPECTED_SOURCE` and
`PPSV_BACKUP_EXPECTED_SOURCE`. Leave
`PPSV_SERVICE_IDENTITY_AUTHORIZED_ACK`, `PPSV_TICKET_E2E_TEST_ACK`, and
`PPSV_POOL_SNAPSHOT_POLICY_ACK` at `0` until the corresponding gate has real
evidence. Production verification deliberately fails while any remains `0`.

## Install and preflight Shiny Server

Review the current [Posit platform support
matrix](https://docs.posit.co/platform-support.html) and [Shiny Server
documentation](https://docs.posit.co/shiny-server/). The repository gate
expects Ubuntu 26.04 on `amd64`; it stops on an unsupported OS or architecture.
Do not force a partial installation on a mismatched host.

Obtain the chosen Shiny Server `.deb` through the approved administrator
channel, independently review its SHA-256, and install it explicitly:

```bash
sudo scripts/install_shiny_server.sh \
  --env /root/ppsvf-app.env \
  --deb /absolute/path/shiny-server-1.5.23.1030-amd64.deb
```

The sample environment pins the reviewed official checksum. The installer
validates package name, exact version, Ubuntu release, package/host
architecture, and checksum. It never downloads a package.

## Provision idempotently

Mount the project pool and external backup destination first, then run:

```bash
sudo scripts/provision.sh --env /root/ppsvf-app.env --install-system
```

Provisioning validates TLS and both external mount identities before copying or
changing configuration, creates the private runtime account and persistent
paths, applies the pool ACL, installs Apache/Shiny templates and systemd units,
and enables the mail and backup timers. Re-running the command with the same
reviewed inputs is supported.

## Deploy an immutable release

The repository must contain `ppsvf-app/renv.lock` and should be clean and
traceable to a commit:

```bash
cd /home/yeroslaviz/BCFPPCF-project-management
sudo scripts/deploy.sh --source "$PWD"
```

The deploy command:

1. stages code in a new release directory;
2. restores the locked R environment;
3. verifies `rJava` and `mailR`;
4. creates a verified pre-deployment database/fallback backup when a database
   already exists;
5. stops workers, creates a fresh PPSV database only when absent, and applies
   later migrations transactionally;
6. atomically points `/srv/shiny-server/ppsvf-app` at the release; and
7. starts services and runs local deployment checks.

It never imports or migrates `ms_projects.db`.

## Verify before handoff

Run the automated verifier with normal certificate validation:

```bash
sudo scripts/verify_deployment.sh
```

For an authenticated route test, create a temporary mode-`0600` curl netrc
containing a dedicated LDAP test account, then run:

```bash
sudo scripts/verify_deployment.sh \
  --netrc /root/ppsv-test.netrc \
  --role-user ORDINARY_LDAP_USERNAME
sudo shred -u /root/ppsv-test.netrc
```

Do not use `curl -k`. Complete the browser, WebSocket, role, ticket, pool, and
restore checks in [Acceptance and handoff](acceptance.qmd) before signing off.

## Routine operator commands

```bash
# Process mail immediately in addition to the one-minute timer.
sudo systemctl start ppsv-mail-outbox.service

# Reconcile checksum-verified fallback uploads after the pool returns.
sudo systemctl start ppsv-pool-reconcile.service

# Create the nightly-style verified backup immediately.
sudo systemctl start ppsv-backup.service

# Inspect recent unit logs.
sudo journalctl -u shiny-server.service -u ppsv-mail-outbox.service \
  -u ppsv-backup.service --since today
```

## Stop conditions

Stop and investigate instead of weakening the system if any of these occur:

- TLS key, leaf certificate, SAN, expiry, or chain validation fails;
- the VM is not the reviewed OS/architecture combination;
- the project pool or external backup destination is not mounted;
- the runtime account cannot create `2770` directories and `0660` files;
- Apache is not the only public route to Shiny;
- LDAP identity can be supplied through a query string, cookie, or client
  header;
- the dependency lock cannot be restored cleanly; or
- a backup cannot be verified or restored on a disposable test target.
